answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when its claims fail independent checks. A sable account cannot gain extra votes merely by minting more names: every identity must lock the same meaningful bond, and a cipher commitment can bind the bond to one account without exposing it publicly. If a jade-backed agent is caught coordinating fraud, its bond is forfeited, so a Sybil attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it.
